correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation of the exact phase primitive establishes a pathwise identity with no residual term at reset boundaries. Stationary length-biased cycle with uniform phase and nonlattice renewal convergence yields two asymptotically independent potentials; product moments give the iff duration moment cutoff for all q>0. Under finite third duration moment covariance tends to zero and yields exact t^-2 time-average variance; if it fails, Portmanteau implies the unscaled integrated variance diverges. Exact rational checks for four polynomial observables and an independent stationary exponential-clock simulation substantiate the algebra; neither substitutes for the renewal-theorem proof. No unproved infinite-range numerical assertion is made.

value.rationale: The source establishes one-point uniformity but not what an observer learns from long time-integrated position measurements. The newly found all-observable coboundary forces an exceptional absence of ordinary occupation CLT noise, supplies an explicit full unscaled limit law and a sharp inverse-speed moment boundary, including finite-versus-divergent variance across E[T^3]. These are meaningful directly observable transport facts for the exact stationary model, not a tiny parameter refinement or arbitrary small-system census.
